title: Component dimensions at Hilbert--Samuel near points, including nilpotents
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, locally closed in a smooth finite-type $\mathbf Q$-scheme; no reducedness is assumed [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For $u\in X$ define $h_{X,u}(n)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,u}/\mathfrak m_u^{n+1})$, $t_u=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbf Q}\kappa(u)$, $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{i=0}^n f(i)$, and $H_X(u)=\Lambda^{t_u}h_{X,u}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length] [def-kun-transcendence-degree] [def-weil-residue-field]. Irreducible components and their dimensions refer to the underlying topological space [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Write $P_X(u)=\{\dim Z:u\in Z,\ Z\text{ an irreducible component of }X\}$. Let $C\hookrightarrow X$ be a smooth closed center on which $H_X$ is locally constant, and let $X^\prime$ be the scheme-theoretic strict transform in the ambient blowup along $C$ [def-nagata-global-blowup] [def-nagata-strict-transform]. For $y\in X^\prime$ over $x\in C$, one has $P_{X^\prime}(y)\subseteq P_X(x)$. If $H_{X^\prime}(y)=H_X(x)$, then $P_{X^\prime}(y)=P_X(x)$. Components contained in $C$ may disappear; the equality hypothesis is essential.

The retained-profile assertion also holds for the finite tests of a local Hilbert--Samuel presentation [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-presentation]. Precisely, start on a neighbourhood where $H_X\le H_0$ and where $P_X=P_0$ on the $H_0$ equality locus, with an actual presentation of $H_0$. Take any finite admissible test sequence of that presentation, retaining ordered earlier-center ideals separately from its initially empty test boundary. At a prefix let $r$ count its affine-line products and let $X_j$ denote its transformed scheme, with strict transform for an admissible blowup and the prescribed cartesian pullbacks for the auxiliary tests. At every point $y$ retaining the extended level, $H_{X_j}(y)=\Lambda^r H_0$, one has $P_{X_j}(y)=P_0+r:=\{d+r:d\in P_0\}$. Locally along this retaining locus one can restrict to neighbourhoods on which $H_{X_j}\le\Lambda^rH_0$ and $P_{X_j}\subseteq P_0+r$. This is conditional on a supplied test sequence and presentation; it asserts no existence of a presentation, normalized invariant or resolution tower.

source.place: BMT arXiv:0905.3580v1, §6.3, Gabber dimension-profile correction and Remark 6.2 (pp.14--15), using §6.1 for the extended function and §6.2 for tests. Online source read at https://arxiv.org/html/0905.3580v1; local archival PDF WANTED. No Stacks tag states this component-retention assertion.

proof.text: Work locally where the embedding is closed. The finite-type scheme is Noetherian and has finitely many components. For ANY center, the strict transform is the scheme-theoretic closure of the unchanged open $X\setminus C$. Its underlying space is therefore the union of the closures of $Z\setminus C$, for components $Z$ not contained in $C$. These irreducible closures are distinct and incomparable, since restricting a containment to the preserved open would contain one original component in another. They are exactly the components upstairs. Nilpotents do not alter this topological calculation. Each such closure maps into $Z$, so one through $y$ comes from a $Z$ through $x$. The preserved dense open identifies their function fields; finite-type domain dimension equals their common transcendence degree. Hence $P_{X^\prime}(y)\subseteq P_X(x)$ without an equality assumption. Finite type upstairs follows also from the finite Rees charts, generated by finitely many fractions of center generators.

proof.text: Now assume equality of the extended functions. Apply [lem-per-scheme-near-point-normal-cone] to obtain $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $I=\mathcal I_{C,x}$, $A=R/I$, $k=\kappa(x)$, $G=\operatorname{gr}_I R$ flat over $A$, and $S=G\otimes_Ak\simeq B[T_1,\ldots,T_e]$, with $y$ in the vertex subspace $\operatorname{Proj}k[T_1,\ldots,T_e]$. The source center is smooth and its extended function locally constant, just as required. This new statement allows nilpotents and arbitrary residue extensions; the reduced version in lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-near-normal-cone cannot be used. In the following two steps we use only this flatness and polynomial decomposition, not regularity of $A$.

source.place: BMT arXiv:0905.3580v1, §6.3, Gabber dimension-profile correction and Remark 6.2 (pp.14--15), using §6.1 for the extended function and §6.2 for tests. Online source read at https://arxiv.org/html/0905.3580v1; local archival PDF WANTED. No Stacks tag states this component-retention assertion.

proof.text: Fix a minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$. For $\bar I=(I+\mathfrak p)/\mathfrak p$ let $q:S\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_{\bar I}(R/\mathfrak p)\otimes_Ak$. Degree $n$ of $S$ is $I^n/\mathfrak mI^n$, and degree $n$ of the target is $(I^n+\mathfrak p)/(\mathfrak mI^n+\mathfrak p)$, because $I\subset\mathfrak m$. Thus a homogeneous kernel element has representative $a\in I^n\cap\mathfrak p$. Let $\epsilon:S\to k[T_1,\ldots,T_e]$ be the vertex quotient. If its image is nonzero, $n>0$ and the polynomial-vertex regularity lemma makes multiplication by the kernel element injective on $S$. The flat graded-fibre lift then makes $a$ a nonzerodivisor in $R$. But the minimal-prime associatedness lemma supplies a nonzero $z$ with annihilator $\mathfrak p$, so $az=0$, a contradiction. Therefore $\ker q\subseteq\ker\epsilon$, first homogeneously and then by finite homogeneous decomposition. This works without reducedness and without regularity of $A$.

source.place: BMT arXiv:0905.3580v1, §6.3, Gabber dimension-profile correction and Remark 6.2 (pp.14--15), using §6.1 for the extended function and §6.2 for tests. proof.text: The exceptional fibre of the strict transform of the reduced component $Z$ corresponding to $\mathfrak p$ is $\operatorname{Proj}(\operatorname{gr}_{\bar I}(R/\mathfrak p)\otimes_Ak)$. Indeed its intrinsic blowup is the ambient strict transform; coefficientwise base change of its Rees algebra to $k$ gives this graded ring, since $\bar I^n\otimes_Rk=(\bar I^n/\bar I^{n+1})\otimes_Ak$. The kernel inclusion of step 3 puts the entire vertex subspace in this fibre. Thus $y$ lies on the strict transform of EVERY component through $x$. A component contained in $C$ would give a graded ring with zero positive degrees and empty Proj, so cannot occur at such a $y$. Step 1 identifies their dimensions and proves equality of profiles. This also proves the same component-incidence conclusion whenever the flat polynomial-cone data of steps 2-3 are supplied by another ideal, even if its quotient is not regular.

proof.text: For a supplied finite test sequence put $L_j=\Lambda^{r_j}H_0$. Use [lem-per-retained-test-boundary-regularity] for the bound $H_j\le L_j$, regularity of its freshly created boundary, and the no-return assertion for exceptional tests. At a line test $H_{j+1}=\Lambda H_j$ by the Taylor free-variable formula, so equality implies equality downstairs: finite differences cancel summation. At an admissible blowup its center lies in the retaining locus, so points above the center have retaining images; off the center the map is an isomorphism. At exceptional-intersection tests retaining images are supplied by the new boundary lemma. Consequently a point retaining $L_j$ has retaining ancestors at EVERY prefix. This is the inductive invariant; its depth-zero profile is $P_0$ by hypothesis. Ordered earlier-center ideals never enter the fresh test boundary.

source.place: BMT arXiv:0905.3580v1, §6.3, Gabber dimension-profile correction and Remark 6.2 (pp.14--15), using §6.1 for the extended function and §6.2 for tests. Online source read at https://arxiv.org/html/0905.3580v1; local archival PDF WANTED. No Stacks tag states this component-retention assertion.

proof.text: At an admissible blowup, the source retaining locus is exactly the cosupport of the transformed presentation. Hence its smooth center has constant $H_j=L_j$ locally. For a retaining point upstairs, steps 2-4 applied to this actual strict transform preserve its entire dimension profile. Off the center use the preserved open. At a line product every component is $Z\times\mathbf A^1$, of dimension $\dim Z+1$: on affine domains its function field is $\mathbf Q(Z)(T)$, so use dimension equals transcendence degree and the tower formula. The components through a point correspond to those through its image, since a polynomial ring over a domain is a domain and contraction of the point detects exactly which component ideals it contains. The free-variable formula gives the extended level $\Lambda L_j$. Thus the inductive profile becomes exactly $P_0+r_j+1$ at a line test.

source.place: BMT arXiv:0905.3580v1, §6.3, Gabber dimension-profile correction and Remark 6.2 (pp.14--15), using §6.1 for the extended function and §6.2 for tests. Online source read at https://arxiv.org/html/0905.3580v1; local archival PDF WANTED. No Stacks tag states this component-retention assertion.

proof.text: At an exceptional-intersection test with retaining source $x$, let $a,b$ be the equations of its two boundary hypersurfaces in $R=\mathcal O_{X_j,x}$. They are a regular sequence by [lem-per-retained-test-boundary-regularity]. The ambient blowup charts after cartesian pullback are $R[v]/(av-b)$ and $R[w]/(bw-a)$. The regular-sequence blowup-chart lemma identifies these with the intrinsic charts $R[(a,b)/a]$ and $R[(a,b)/b]$; thus the cartesian model is locally the intrinsic blowup, including nilpotents, near this fibre. Also $G=\operatorname{gr}_{(a,b)}R\simeq (R/(a,b))[T_1,T_2]$ by the regular-sequence graded-polynomial theorem. It is flat over $R/(a,b)$, with polynomial fibre $k[T_1,T_2]$. Take $B=k$ in the argument of steps 3-4: its vertex subspace is the WHOLE exceptional fibre. Therefore every component through $x$ has strict transform through every point of this fibre. Step 1 gives dimension preservation and excludes extra components. This proves the induction at auxiliary tests using the specified cartesian transform, without assuming that the center is smooth inside $X_j$.

source.place: BMT arXiv:0905.3580v1, §6.3, Gabber dimension-profile correction and Remark 6.2 (pp.14--15), using §6.1 for the extended function and §6.2 for tests. Online source read at https://arxiv.org/html/0905.3580v1; local archival PDF WANTED. No Stacks tag states this component-retention assertion.

proof.text: Steps 5-7 prove by induction on the finite test length that every retaining point has profile $P_0+r_j$. For the local neighbourhood assertion, apply closed upper level sets and finite image of the scheme Hilbert--Samuel theorem to the current finite-type scheme: the locus $H_j\le L_j$ is open (if any greater values occur, exclude the closed upper set of their least one). At a retaining $y$, remove the finitely many closed components not containing $y$. Every remaining component has dimension in $P_{X_j}(y)=P_0+r_j$; at every point of this open neighbourhood the profile is therefore a subset of that set. Intersect the two opens. The empty retaining locus is vacuous. The proof constructs no presentation, invariant or resolution tower; it only follows the supplied finite sequence.
